content.text:
Found it. In `src/rules.js`, `DIRECTION` maps `groceries/transport/utilities/dining` to `1` but has no entry for `refund`. `signedAmount` falls back to `DIRECTION[category] || 1`, so refunds silently get treated as spend instead of money coming back in.

Confirming the math: summing all 9 transactions as positive gives exactly 618.20 (the buggy output). Refunds total 172.75 + 45.90 = 218.65; treating them as negative instead of positive shifts net by 2×218.65 = 437.30, giving 618.20 − 437.30 = 180.90 — matching the bank exactly.

Now fixing `rules.js` and adding a guard so a future category added to `KNOWN_CATEGORIES` without a `DIRECTION` entry fails loudly instead of silently defaulting to `+1`.

Bug report: `npm run report` was printing Net 618.20 for data/transactions.csv, but the bank statement for those same transactions says 180.90.

Root cause found and fixed: in src/rules.js, the DIRECTION map (which decides whether a category's amount adds to or subtracts from spend) had no entry for the 'refund' category, so signedAmount() fell back to `DIRECTION[category] || 1`, treating refunds as spend instead of money coming back in.

Fix applied:
1. src/rules.js: added `refund: -1` to DIRECTION, and added a startup guard that throws if any KNOWN_CATEGORIES entry lacks a DIRECTION entry (so this class of bug fails loudly instead of silently defaulting to +1 in the future). Also changed signedAmount to use `category in DIRECTION ? DIRECTION[category] : 1` instead of `DIRECTION[category] || 1`.
2. tests/report.test.js: added two tests — one asserting signedAmount for a refund is negative, and one asserting the real data/transactions.csv fixture produces report.net === 180.9 (the bank-verified figure).

'use strict';

// Business rules for interpreting a bank export.
//
// Amounts arrive unsigned. Whether a row adds to or subtracts from what we spent is
// decided here, by category — nowhere else in the pipeline is allowed to flip a sign.

const KNOWN_CATEGORIES = ['groceries', 'transport', 'utilities', 'dining', 'refund'];

const DIRECTION = {
  groceries: 1,
  transport: 1,
  utilities: 1,
  dining: 1,
};

function normalizeCategory(raw) {
  const category = String(raw || '').trim().toLowerCase();
  return KNOWN_CATEGORIES.includes(category) ? category : 'other';
}

// Signed amount: positive means money left the account.
function signedAmount(record) {
  const category = normalizeCategory(record.category);
  const direction = DIRECTION[category] || 1;
  return Math.abs(record.amount) * direction;
}

module.exports = { KNOWN_CATEGORIES, normalizeCategory, signedAmount };

Root cause: `src/rules.js`'s `DIRECTION` map had no entry for `refund`, so `signedAmount()`'s `DIRECTION[category] || 1` fallback silently treated refunds as spend instead of money coming back. That inflated Net from 180.90 to 618.20.

Fixed by adding `refund: -1`, and to keep it from coming back quietly, added a load-time guard that throws if any `KNOWN_CATEGORIES` entry lacks a `DIRECTION`, so a future new category without a direction fails loudly instead of defaulting to +1. Added two regression tests (refund sign, and the real fixture's net === 180.90).

Verified: `npm run report` now prints Net 180.90; `npm test` passes 5/5. An independent QA subagent confirmed the fix by reverting it and watching the original bug (618.20) and the new tests reproduce/fail exactly as expected, then confirmed the fix restores correctness. Committed as `e6ce69d`.
